newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SOUNESS BACK ON FAMILIAR TERRITORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUNESS BACK ON FAMILIAR TERRITORY.

text.p: Graeme Souness will return to Anfield for the first time in two-and-a-half years on Saturday to find his former assistant Roy Evans and the current Liverpool side reluctant to lay out the welcome mat on the pitch.

Souness, who parted company with Liverpool during the 1993-94 season after managing the club he had previously played for with distinction, is now in charge of Southampton after a spell with Galatasaray who won the Turkish Cup under his command.
But Evans, assistant manager in Souness's regime, will not allow sentiment to cloud the main issue of maintaining Liverpool's unbeaten record in the English premiership so far.

"You wish him success but not at Anfield," said Evans. "Come three o'clock I won't be worrying about Southampton or being friendly to Graeme Souness. That sort of thing is great before and after but when the game is on he's just another manager.
"He will always be welcome at Liverpool in my eyes. I enjoyed working with him. But he's at a different club now."
League leaders Sheffield Wednesday, with four straight wins, will have their confidence tested when third-placed Chelsea visit Hillsborough.

Wednesday manager David Pleat does not have the spending power enjoyed by Ruud Gullit but believes his young side will prove their worth against expensive imports Gianluca Vialli, Roberto Di Matteo and Frank Leboeuf.
Second-placed Aston Villa tackle Arsenal, currently fifth, in another game which could indicate which of the two sides' is more likely to remain in the upper reaches of the table.
Manager Brian Little, though, is concerned about the schedule which confronts his side as well as other clubs in Europe.
"With the fixtures ahead, I can't see anyone getting a day off. We've got a hell of a task this month and it is not going to get any easier," said Little.
Newcastle will be looking for more inspiration from back-in-favour Peter Beardsley, who scored in the 2-1 win over Sunderland in midweek, as they take on Tottenham at White Hart Lane.
Leeds meet Manchester United in a traditionally fierce encounter, while Middlesborough's team of exotic imports are at home to bottom club Coventry.
Wimbledon tackle Everton in a match currently overshadowed by Vinnie Jones's latest dismissal, the 12th of his career, in the 1-0 win over Tottenham on Wednesday.
Jones, who will receive a one-match ban, alleges he was provoked because he thought England's Darren Anderton had spat at him.
"Yesterday I was rounding up stray cows at my smallholding and they behaved better than Anderton," said Jones, fined by the F.A. last season for comparing Gullit to "a squealing, pot-bellied pig."
Anderton admits he did spit, but not deliberately at Jones. "Footballers spit all the time and when I turned my head to clear my throat he ran into it."
